## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best swell direction. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best swell direction.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best tide.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Nine sources from eight publishers; seven were read, and the two Surfertoday pages are kept as search-only. Dated sources for this sand-bottom break: Wikipedia 2026, Wikivoyage 2026, Surf Atlas 2024, WSL 2022, Surfer Factory 2021. SWELL DIRECTION CONFLICT, now clearer: Surf-Forecast says W (270, outside the profile window). Backyard Hotel gives SW/W for the main peak, and Surfertoday (search-only) SW/W. Surf Atlas gives S-SW, and Surfer Factory gives S/SW for Almendro. Peaks along the 10-12 km beach differ (the Backyard Hotel page lists W for Tulin and Roca Loca). The profile's optimal 190-230 is supported by Surf Atlas and the Almendro entries. Surf-Forecast's 'west' and the hotel's SW/W suggest extending the optimal window towards 250-260. WIND: NE offshore (Surf-Forecast, Surfertoday) and 'easterly offshores' (Surf Atlas), consistent with the profile's 50. TIDE: mid-to-high is supported for the main peaks (Backyard Hotel, Surf Atlas Almendros, Surfer Factory Almendro), matching the profile. Some peaks (Terraza, Tulin) prefer lower tides. SIZE CONFLICT: Surf Atlas gives ideal 5-9 ft with closeouts above 12 ft at Almendros. Backyard Hotel says the beach tends to close out at about 8 ft+. The profile maximum of 12 ft may be high for the beach itself. PERIOD: no numbers; only 'mostly groundswells'. SEASON: wet season May-October (Surf Atlas) and April-November (Surfertoday, search-only), consistent with the profile's April-October. Several sources stress year-round consistency. The Surf-Forecast guide places it in 'Golfo de Nicoya', but its nearest airports (Quepos 54 km, SJO 64 km) match the Jaco-area Playa Hermosa, not the Guanacaste one.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 5 ft | documented | S5 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 5–9 ft | documented | S5 | no separate setting; working range 3–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 12 ft [S5] · 8 ft [S6] | conflicting | S3, S5, S6 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: The Surf Atlas says the Almendros peak needs 5-9 ft to work at least; the scale is not stated and it refers to one peak of the long beach.
  - S5 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “It’s a very high quality wave that needs 5-9 foot to work at least. That’s the sweet spot cos anything more than 12 and it’ll just slam shut and close out.”
- **Ideal range**: The Surf Atlas gives ideal conditions as the 5-9 ft range and calls 5-9 ft the sweet spot at Almendros; the scale is not stated.
  - S5 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “Ideal conditions are something in the 5-9 foot range with good easterly offshores and medium S-SW swells, usually in the wet season.”
  - S5 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “It’s a very high quality wave that needs 5-9 foot to work at least. That’s the sweet spot cos anything more than 12 and it’ll just slam shut and close out.”
- **Maximum suitable**: The Surf Atlas says Almendros closes out above 12 ft, while the Backyard Hotel says Hermosa tends to close out at 8 (written 8”+, probably feet); Surfertoday (search summary) says waves can reach 13 ft, which is not a working limit.
  - S5 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “It’s a very high quality wave that needs 5-9 foot to work at least. That’s the sweet spot cos anything more than 12 and it’ll just slam shut and close out.”
  - S6 (Backyard Hotel): “Hermosa tends to close out at 8”+”
  - S3 (Surfertoday): “Here, waves can reach 13 feet, and there are always plenty of barrels and punchy lips.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: The Surf Atlas says Almendros closes out above 12 ft, while the Backyard Hotel says Hermosa tends to close out at 8 (written 8”+, probably feet); Surfertoday (search summary) says waves can reach 13 ft, which is not a working limit.
- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast says west, the Backyard Hotel (main peak) and Surfertoday (search summary) southwest/west, and the Surf Atlas and Surfer Factory (Almendro peak) south/southwest; the sources may describe different peaks along the beach.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore winds blow from the northeast and Surfertoday (search summary) gives a northeast wind, while the Surf Atlas speaks of good easterly offshores.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: The Surf Atlas (Almendros), the Backyard Hotel (main peak) and Surfer Factory (Almendro) say mid tide and up, while Surfertoday (search summary) gives a high-tide preference.
